subject: Retry/backoff defaults for SDK helper (streaming + 429 behavior) for Quickstart templates
body:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Retry/backoff defaults for SDK helper (streaming + 429 behavior) for Quickstart templates

Alex — we need to lock retry/backoff + timeout defaults for the SDK helper that the quickstart templates will use (Python + TS). Right now, templates are inconsistent and Support is already flagging 429 confusion + streaming disconnects.

I put a concrete proposal below (and attached a short defaults doc). Main decisions:
1) What we retry for non-streaming vs streaming
2) What “safe defaults” should be (so templates don’t teach bad patterns)
3) Small API tweaks we may want (Retry-After semantics + request_id/trace propagation)

PROPOSED DEFAULTS (SDK helper)

A) Non-streaming requests (chat/completions, embeddings, rerank)
- Timeouts:
  - connect: 5s
  - request total: 60s (configurable)
- Retries (max_attempts=3 => 2 retries):
  - retry on: 408, 409? (NO), 425? (NO), 429, 500, 502, 503, 504
  - do NOT retry on: 400/401/403/404/422
  - backoff: exponential starting 250ms, multiplier 2.0, full jitter, cap 8s
  - always respect Retry-After header if present (prefer server guidance)
- Idempotency:
  - add automatic Idempotency-Key header when caller doesn’t provide one (UUID per request)
  - include x-redwood-client-request-id in logs/trace attrs for correlation

B) Streaming requests
- Timeouts:
  - connect: 5s
  - “time to first token”: 20s (configurable)
  - idle read timeout: 30s (configurable)
- Retries:
  - retry ONLY if disconnect happens before ANY content bytes are received (pre-first-event)
  - if partial stream received, do not auto-retry (risk duplicate tool calls / duplicate tokens)
  - instead: raise a typed StreamingInterrupted error with guidance:
    - “If you need to reissue, reuse the same Idempotency-Key and client_request_id; do not retry tool actions unless you de-dup on your side.”

Why this shape:
- aligns with SRE guidance (avoid retry storms; respect server Retry-After; keep caps low)
- avoids teaching unsafe “always retry streaming” patterns
- gives templates a consistent story across languages

API/PLATFORM TWEAKS REQUEST (small, but helps a lot)
- Ensure Retry-After is always set on 429 (seconds) and ideally also return retry_after_ms in error JSON.
- Ensure request id is always echoed back:
  - request header: x-redwood-client-request-id (sent by SDK)
  - response header: x-redwood-request-id (generated server-side)
- Ensure trace context propagation:
  - accept and pass through traceparent (we join client->server traces in Console)

Can you confirm you’re OK with these defaults as “template contract”? If yes, I’ll have teams land the helpers in both SDKs this week and update template READMEs to match.

Attachment: sdk-helper-retry-defaults-v0.4.md

—
Monica Patel
SDK Lead, Redwood Inference



From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 10:01 AM PST
Subject: Re: Retry/backoff defaults for SDK helper (streaming + 429 behavior) for Quickstart templates

This is directionally right.

Two questions before I say “lock it”:
1) For non-streaming, are we sure max 2 retries is enough for noisy networks + occasional capacity blips? (I like low retry counts but want to ensure we don’t regress activation.)
2) Streaming: can we also explicitly document that “tool calls are side-effectful; do not auto-retry after tool execution”? We’ve seen folks accidentally double-charge external APIs.

On API tweaks: +1. Let’s make it minimal and crisp so Henry/Nikhil can accept quickly.

If you can answer (1) with any data (even anecdotal), I’m fine committing this as the template contract.

-Alex



From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 11:07 AM PST
Subject: Re: Retry/backoff defaults for SDK helper (streaming + 429 behavior) for Quickstart templates

Re (1): we pulled a quick snapshot from template dogfood runs + the first batch of support reports.

- The dominant failures are:
  a) 401/invalid key (no retry)
  b) 429 burst (retry helps, but needs to respect Retry-After)
  c) streaming disconnects behind proxies (retrying after partial stream is harmful)
- For 5xx capacity blips, almost all recovered within 1 retry when using exponential backoff with jitter.
- The cases where 2 retries weren’t enough were usually 429 with no server guidance; that’s why I’m pushing hard on “always set Retry-After” +/or include retry_after_ms.

I attached a screenshot of the quick breakout (“failure modes”) — it’s not perfect but enough to justify keeping retry attempts low.

Re (2): yes, we can add explicit language + a typed error that includes a “safe retry hint” in the message. In TS SDK we can include a property like:

- error.retryable: boolean
- error.retryAfterMs?: number
- error.class: 'rate_limit' | 'timeout' | 'stream_interrupted' | ...

And for streaming interrupted after partial output:
- retryable=false
- class=stream_interrupted
- message includes “If you need to reissue: de-dup tool actions; reuse Idempotency-Key.”

Naomi — any security/compliance concerns with auto-generating Idempotency-Key? (It’s just a UUID, no PII.)

Attachments:
- quickstart-template-failure-modes-jan2026.png

—Monica



From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 11:26 AM PST
Subject: Re: Retry/backoff defaults for SDK helper (streaming + 429 behavior) for Quickstart templates

Auto-generating an Idempotency-Key UUID is fine.

Two asks from Security:
- Please ensure the SDK never logs request/response bodies by default (especially in retry paths). It’s common for people to turn on “debug” and accidentally emit prompts.
- If you add error objects, confirm they don’t include raw headers wholesale (headers can carry auth tokens if users misconfigure proxies). Safer to whitelist the bits we want (request_id, retry_after_ms, status, error_class).

On tool calls: strongly agree with making “no auto-retry after partial stream” a hard stance.

-Naomi



From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 2:44 PM PST
Subject: Re: Retry/backoff defaults for SDK helper (streaming + 429 behavior) for Quickstart templates

Great — we’ll keep error objects sanitized (whitelist only) and default logging to metadata only.

Re Alex Q1: given above, I recommend we keep max_attempts=3 (2 retries) as the default, but allow templates to override via env/config for advanced users:
- REDWOOD_SDK_MAX_ATTEMPTS (default 3)
- REDWOOD_SDK_TIMEOUT_MS (default 60000)

We can point people at “increase attempts carefully” guidance in docs, but we don’t want templates to become a retry storm generator.

API tweak request (draft wording we’ll send to Henry/Nikhil):
1) 429 responses MUST include Retry-After header (seconds). If upstream can’t compute, set a conservative value (e.g., 1–2s) rather than omitting.
2) Add retry_after_ms field to error JSON for 429 (optional but preferred).
3) Always echo x-redwood-request-id response header. Accept x-redwood-client-request-id request header.
4) Accept traceparent and ensure it is used for trace linking (no behavior change for customers, just better observability).

If you’re OK, I’ll proceed with implementation in both SDKs and open the small API PR request.

—Monica



From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 22, 2026 at 3:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Retry/backoff defaults for SDK helper (streaming + 429 behavior) for Quickstart templates

Approved.

Please do two things:
- Add a short “Why we don’t auto-retry streams” section to the template contract doc (tool side-effects + duplicate outputs). This will save Support.
- Make sure we surface request_id prominently in exceptions. When users paste stack traces into tickets, we want request_id right there.

Go ahead and send the API tweak request to Henry/Nikhil. Keep it scoped.

-Alex



From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 24, 2026 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: Retry/backoff defaults for SDK helper (streaming + 429 behavior) for Quickstart templates

Quick update / closing the loop:

- Defaults are now written up as “SDK helper retry/timeout contract” and referenced from ENG-2847.
- Python SDK draft PR is ready (adds:
  - max_attempts default=3
  - exponential backoff + jitter
  - respects Retry-After
  - streaming: retry only pre-first-event
  - errors include request_id + error_class + retry_after_ms when available)
- TS SDK draft PR mirrors the behavior + adds typed errors (retryable flag).
- Security asks applied (no body logging by default; error header fields are whitelisted).

I emailed Henry/Nikhil the 4 API tweaks (Retry-After on 429, retry_after_ms field, request_id echo, traceparent).

Next: once Henry confirms feasibility, we’ll align naming (header casing) so templates can reference consistently.

—
Monica Patel
SDK Lead, Redwood Inference
